I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou best, because that is the most familiar and reliable way for me to earn from one piece of land in a year. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage that through harvest first, then I will plant summer maize right after. I will not spread myself across many crops, because at my age I want a system I know well, with steady yield, simple field work, and no need to learn complicated new practices. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put most of my fertilizer into the base application and key growth stages, irrigate only when the crop really needs it, and keep pesticide sprays limited to the main disease and insect pressure. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing every time, and it works well for this rotation.
